ji_apt.t: Federal complaint against US Senate candidate Dan J. Sullivan filed by national GOP-aligned group — Juneau Independent (2026-09-09)

apm_inv.t: State of Alaska opens investigation into second Dan Sullivan's U.S. Senate run — Alaska Public Media (2026-06-09)

checks.legal: Ballot litigation (he prevailed) documented through AP, Alaska Beacon and Alaska Public Media; CourtListener/Justia and Alaska CourtView not searched directly. News searches found no criminal or civil cases against him. A pending FEC complaint is recorded under 'complaints' (not a legal finding).
checks.foreign: None found in news; Senate eFD unreachable. Exact-name check of the DOJ FARA bulk files (registrants, short forms, foreign principals), searched 2026-10-13: no row names this candidate (a 'Daniel J. Sullivan III' of SST Aerospace, Greenville SC, filed a 2019 short form — different person, different suffix and state).
checks.claims: Campaign website not opened. Bio sample = checkable claims in his Alaska Beacon voter-guide answers (4 rated). Campaign sample = his main public statements on his candidacy (filing rules, no coordination, branding) plus one checkable platform claim (Typhoon Halong reimbursement). No ads documented. Fewer than 10 issue claims exist in sources reached.
checks.democracy: Never held office; statements from AP and his Beacon questionnaire.

research_notes: DATA WARNING: this candidate's records profile mixes in Sen. Dan S. Sullivan's FEC ID S4AK00214 (all 2014–2026 cycle totals except the $18,835 row) and the senator's 2021 certification votes. Those belong to the senator, not to Dan J. Sullivan; do not score them here. His own committee (S6AK00326) raised $18,835 through Jul 29, 2026, above the $5,000 threshold that triggers a Senate candidate financial disclosure; eFD was unreachable, so disclosures stays 'no'. Pending matters (not findings): an Americans for Public Trust FEC complaint (Sept. 2026) alleging coordination with 907 Initiative, which the group denies; the Lt. Governor's June 2026 good-faith inquiry, after which the Alaska Supreme Court ruled him eligible. An Alaska Beacon headline (Sept. 9, 2026) says Trump indicated DOJ may bring a case against him; the page could not be opened and no filed case was found.
